mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship is consistent across the current monetary policy cycle.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.5% (as measured by the trailing 3-month average).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (exceeding 0.3 percentage points in three months) signals deteriorating labor market conditions and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE rise > 0.3pp in 3 months).

mechanism_narrative: The positive impact of a low federal funds rate on equity returns is amplified when the unemployment rate is low, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. This interaction effect is strongest in periods of stable economic growth.
failure_condition: The interaction term between FEDFUNDS and UNRATE has a negative coefficient in a regression of 60-day returns, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion characterized by strong housing starts (HOUST > 1300) and robust industrial production (INDPRO > 100), the S&P 500 produces positive forward returns as the economy approaches its peak, reflecting continued corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST > 1300 and INDPRO > 100.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) signals robust manufacturing activity and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. This relationship holds consistently in the current economic cycle.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO increases by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in retail sales (RSAFS falling more than 0.5% in three months) indicates weakening consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (RSAFS decline > 0.5% in 3 months).

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) combined with robust consumer spending (RSAFS) amplifies the positive effect on equity returns, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This interaction is most pronounced in early-cycle expansions.
failure_condition: The interaction term between PAYEMS and RSAFS has a negative coefficient in a regression of 20-day returns, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 320) and high interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.0), the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days as the central bank tightens policy to combat inflation.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both CPIAUCSL > 320 and FEDFUNDS > 4.0.
